## **Chapter 158 - Import Processing Pipeline**

### 158.1 Processing Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Start[Import Job Started]
    Start --> Validate[Validation Phase]
    
    Validate --> PreProcess[Pre-Processing]
    PreProcess --> Batch[Batch Creation]
    
    Batch --> Process[Process Batch]
    Process --> ACL[ACL Transformation]
    ACL --> Map[Field Mapping]
    Map --> Resolve[Entity Resolution]
    Resolve --> Enrich[Data Enrichment]
    Enrich --> Create[Entity Creation]
    
    Create --> Success{Success?}
    Success -->|Yes| Record[Record Success]
    Success -->|No| Error[Record Error]
    
    Record --> More{More Records?}
    Error --> More
    
    More -->|Yes| Process
    More -->|No| PostProcess[Post-Processing]
    
    PostProcess --> Relationships[Resolve Relationships]
    Relationships --> Finalize[Finalize Import]
    Finalize --> Complete[Complete]
```

### 158.2 Validation Phase

**Pre-Import Validation:**
```csharp
public class ImportValidator
{
    public async Task<ValidationResult> ValidateAsync(ImportJob job)
    {
        var result = new ValidationResult();
        
        // 1. Validate source connectivity
        var connectionValid = await ValidateSourceConnection(job);
        if (!connectionValid.IsValid)
        {
            result.AddError("Source connection failed", connectionValid.Error);
            return result; // Fatal error
        }
        
        // 2. Validate mapping configuration
        var mappingValid = ValidateMappingConfiguration(job.MappingConfiguration);
        if (!mappingValid.IsValid)
        {
            result.AddErrors(mappingValid.Errors);
        }
        
        // 3. Validate required fields mapped
        var requiredFields = GetRequiredFields(job.Type);
        foreach (var field in requiredFields)
        {
            if (!IsMapped(field, job.MappingConfiguration))
            {
                result.AddError($"Required field not mapped: {field}");
            }
        }
        
        // 4. Validate target entities exist
        if (job.MappingConfiguration.ProjectId.HasValue)
        {
            var projectExists = await _projectRepo.ExistsAsync(
                job.MappingConfiguration.ProjectId.Value);
            if (!projectExists)
            {
                result.AddError("Target project does not exist");
            }
        }
        
        // 5. Validate workflow compatibility
        if (job.MappingConfiguration.WorkflowId.HasValue)
        {
            var workflowValid = await ValidateWorkflowMapping(
                job.MappingConfiguration.WorkflowId.Value,
                job.MappingConfiguration.StatusMappings);
            result.Merge(workflowValid);
        }
        
        // 6. Dry run validation (sample records)
        if (job.IsDryRun || result.IsValid)
        {
            var sampleValidation = await ValidateSampleRecords(job, sampleSize: 100);
            result.Merge(sampleValidation);
        }
        
        return result;
    }
}
```

### 158.3 Batch Processing

**Batch Processor:**
```csharp
public class ImportBatchProcessor
{
    private const int DefaultBatchSize = 500;
    private const int MaxParallelBatches = 5;
    
    public async Task ProcessBatchAsync(ImportJob job, ImportBatch batch)
    {
        var records = await LoadBatchRecords(job, batch);
        var results = new ConcurrentBag<ProcessingResult>();
        
        // Process records in parallel within batch
        await Parallel.ForEachAsync(
            records,
            new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 10 },
            async (record, ct) =>
            {
                var result = await ProcessRecordAsync(job, record);
                results.Add(result);
            });
        
        // Update batch statistics
        batch.SuccessCount = results.Count(r => r.Success);
        batch.FailureCount = results.Count(r => !r.Success);
        batch.ProcessedIds = results
            .Where(r => r.Success)
            .Select(r => r.EntityId.ToString())
            .ToList();
        
        batch.Complete();
        
        // Commit batch
        await _repository.UpdateAsync(batch);
        
        // Emit batch completed event
        await _eventBus.PublishAsync(new ImportBatchCompletedEto
        {
            JobId = job.Id,
            BatchId = batch.Id,
            SuccessCount = batch.SuccessCount,
            FailureCount = batch.FailureCount
        });
    }
    
    private async Task<ProcessingResult> ProcessRecordAsync(
        ImportJob job,
        SourceRecord record)
    {
        try
        {
            // Step 1: ACL transformation
            var transformed = await _acl.TransformAsync(record, job.Source);
            
            // Step 2: Field mapping
            var mapped = await _mapper.MapAsync(
                transformed,
                job.MappingConfiguration);
            
            // Step 3: Entity resolution
            await _resolver.ResolveReferencesAsync(mapped);
            
            // Step 4: Validation
            var validation = await _validator.ValidateEntityAsync(mapped);
            if (!validation.IsValid)
            {
                return ProcessingResult.Failed(
                    record.SourceId,
                    validation.Errors);
            }
            
            // Step 5: Entity creation
            Guid entityId;
            if (job.Type == ImportJobType.Task)
            {
                entityId = await CreateTaskAsync(mapped, job);
            }
            else if (job.Type == ImportJobType.Project)
            {
                entityId = await CreateProjectAsync(mapped, job);
            }
            else
            {
                throw new NotSupportedException($"Type {job.Type} not supported");
            }
            
            // Step 6: Store source mapping
            await StoreSourceMappingAsync(
                sourceSystem: job.Source.ToString(),
                sourceId: record.SourceId,
                targetId: entityId);
            
            return ProcessingResult.Success(record.SourceId, entityId);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to process record {SourceId}", record.SourceId);
            
            await RecordErrorAsync(job, record, ex);
            
            return ProcessingResult.Failed(
                record.SourceId,
                new[] { ex.Message });
        }
    }
}
```

### 158.4 Relationship Resolution Phase

**Purpose:** Handle cross-entity relationships after all entities created.

```csharp
public class RelationshipResolver
{
    public async Task ResolveRelationshipsAsync(ImportJob job)
    {
        // Step 1: Load all source-to-target mappings
        var mappings = await _mappingRepo.GetByJobAsync(job.Id);
        
        // Step 2: Process parent-child relationships
        await ResolveHierarchyAsync(job, mappings);
        
        // Step 3: Process dependencies
        await ResolveDependenciesAsync(job, mappings);
        
        // Step 4: Process links
        await ResolveLinksAsync(job, mappings);
    }
    
    private async Task ResolveHierarchyAsync(
        ImportJob job,
        List<SourceTargetMapping> mappings)
    {
        // Find all records with parent references
        var childRecords = await _sourceRecordRepo
            .FindWithParentReferenceAsync(job.Id);
        
        foreach (var child in childRecords)
        {
            var parentSourceId = child.Fields["parent_key"]?.ToString();
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(parentSourceId))
                continue;
            
            // Find parent's target ID
            var parentMapping = mappings.FirstOrDefault(
                m => m.SourceId == parentSourceId);
            
            if (parentMapping == null)
            {
                _logger.LogWarning(
                    "Parent not found for child {ChildSourceId}: {ParentSourceId}",
                    child.SourceId,
                    parentSourceId);
                continue;
            }
            
            // Set parent relationship
            var childTask = await _taskRepo.GetAsync(child.TargetId);
            childTask.SetParent(parentMapping.TargetId);
            await _taskRepo.UpdateAsync(childTask);
        }
    }
    
    private async Task ResolveDependenciesAsync(
        ImportJob job,
        List<SourceTargetMapping> mappings)
    {
        var dependencyRecords = await _sourceRecordRepo
            .FindWithDependenciesAsync(job.Id);
        
        foreach (var record in dependencyRecords)
        {
            var dependencies = record.Fields["dependencies"] as List<string>;
            if (dependencies?.Any() != true)
                continue;
            
            var task = await _taskRepo.GetAsync(record.TargetId);
            
            foreach (var depSourceId in dependencies)
            {
                var depMapping = mappings.FirstOrDefault(
                    m => m.SourceId == depSourceId);
                
                if (depMapping != null)
                {
                    task.AddDependency(new TaskDependency
                    {
                        DependsOnTaskId = depMapping.TargetId,
                        Type = DependencyType.FinishToStart
                    });
                }
            }
            
            await _taskRepo.UpdateAsync(task);
        }
    }
}
```

### 159.3 Export Processing

```csharp
public class ExportProcessor
{
    public async Task ProcessExportAsync(ExportJob job)
    {
        job.Start();
        await _repository.UpdateAsync(job);
        
        try
        {
            // Step 1: Query data based on scope
            var data = await QueryDataAsync(job.Scope);
            job.TotalRecords = data.Count();
            
            // Step 2: Create output stream
            using var outputStream = await CreateOutputStreamAsync(job);
            
            // Step 3: Write data in batches
            var writer = CreateWriter(job.Format, outputStream);
            
            await foreach (var batch in data.Batch(1000))
            {
                await writer.WriteBatchAsync(batch);
                job.ProcessedRecords += batch.Count();
                
                // Update progress periodically
                if (job.ProcessedRecords % 10000 == 0)
                {
                    await _repository.UpdateAsync(job);
                }
            }
            
            // Step 4: Finalize output
            await writer.FinalizeAsync();
            job.OutputSizeBytes = outputStream.Length;
            
            // Step 5: Handle attachments if requested
            if (job.IncludeAttachments)
            {
                await ExportAttachmentsAsync(job, data);
            }
            
            // Step 6: Create download link
            var downloadUrl = await _storageService.GetDownloadUrlAsync(
                job.OutputPath,
                expiresIn: TimeSpan.FromDays(7));
            
            job.Complete();
            job.ExpiresAt = DateTime.UtcNow.AddDays(7);
            
            await _repository.UpdateAsync(job);
            
            // Notify requester
            await _notificationService.NotifyAsync(
                job.RequestedBy,
                $"Export completed: {downloadUrl}");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Export failed for job {JobId}", job.Id);
            job.Fail();
            await _repository.UpdateAsync(job);
            throw;
        }
    }
}
```

### 160.3 AI-Assisted Mapping

**Auto-Mapping Engine:**
```csharp
public class AutoMappingEngine
{
    public async Task<List<MappingRecommendation>> SuggestMappingsAsync(
        SourceSchema sourceSchema,
        TargetSchema targetSchema)
    {
        var recommendations = new List<MappingRecommendation>();
        
        foreach (var sourceField in sourceSchema.Fields)
        {
            // Exact name match
            var exactMatch = targetSchema.Fields.FirstOrDefault(
                f => f.Name.Equals(sourceField.Name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            
            if (exactMatch != null)
            {
                recommendations.Add(new MappingRecommendation
                {
                    SourceField = sourceField.Name,
                    TargetField = exactMatch.Name,
                    Confidence = 1.0,
                    Reason = "Exact name match"
                });
                continue;
            }
            
            // Semantic similarity (using AI embeddings)
            var semanticMatches = await _aiService.FindSemanticMatchesAsync(
                sourceField,
                targetSchema.Fields);
            
            if (semanticMatches.Any())
            {
                var best = semanticMatches.First();
                recommendations.Add(new MappingRecommendation
                {
                    SourceField = sourceField.Name,
                    TargetField = best.Field.Name,
                    Confidence = best.Similarity,
                    Reason = $"Semantic similarity: {best.Similarity:P0}"
                });
                continue;
            }
            
            // Pattern-based matching
            var pattern = DetectFieldPattern(sourceField);
            if (pattern != null)
            {
                var match = FindPatternMatch(pattern, targetSchema.Fields);
                if (match != null)
                {
                    recommendations.Add(new MappingRecommendation
                    {
                        SourceField = sourceField.Name,
                        TargetField = match.Name,
                        Confidence = 0.7,
                        Reason = $"Pattern match: {pattern}"
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        
        return recommendations;
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 162 - Performance Optimization**

### 162.1 Bulk Import Optimization

**Strategies:**
1. **Batch Processing** - Process 500-1000 records per batch
2. **Parallel Processing** - Multiple batches concurrently (tenant-isolated)
3. **Bulk Insert** - Use database bulk operations where possible
4. **Deferred Validation** - Validate in parallel with processing
5. **Connection Pooling** - Reuse database connections
6. **Memory Management** - Stream large files instead of loading to memory

**Performance Targets:**
- CSV Import: 5,000-10,000 records/minute
- API Import (Jira): 1,000-2,000 records/minute
- Attachment Import: 100-500 files/minute
- Export: 10,000-20,000 records/minute

# **PART XVI - SHARED KERNEL ARCHITECTURE**

## **Chapter 163 - Shared Kernel Philosophy**

### 163.1 What Is a Shared Kernel?

A **Shared Kernel** is a bounded context or sub-domain that is **jointly owned and used by multiple bounded contexts** without modification. It represents:

- **Highly stable** building blocks
- **Domain-agnostic** functionality
- **Reusable** across contexts
- **Strongly consistent** models
- **Version-controlled** interfaces

### 163.2 Shared Kernel vs. Other Integration Patterns

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Patterns ["Integration Patterns"]
        SK[Shared Kernel<br/>Joint ownership<br/>Direct dependency]
        PL[Published Language<br/>Event contracts<br/>Loose coupling]
        CS[Customer-Supplier<br/>API contracts<br/>Upstream/downstream]
        ACL[Anti-Corruption Layer<br/>Translation<br/>Protection]
    end
    
    subgraph Usage ["When to Use"]
        SK --> U1[Core primitives<br/>Universal patterns<br/>High stability]
        PL --> U2[Cross-context events<br/>Async integration<br/>Autonomy]
        CS --> U3[Service consumption<br/>Clear ownership<br/>Stability]
        ACL --> U4[External systems<br/>Legacy integration<br/>Schema mismatch]
    end
```

### 163.3 Shared Kernel Principles

**1. High Cohesion**  
Shared kernels contain only tightly related concepts that truly belong together.

**2. Stability**  
Changes to shared kernels require coordination across all consumers.

**3. Minimal Surface Area**  
Expose only what's necessary; keep implementation details hidden.

**4. No Business Logic**  
Shared kernels contain structure and patterns, not business rules.

**5. Versioning Strategy**  
Breaking changes require major version bumps and migration paths.

**6. Clear Ownership**  
Despite being shared, there's a designated team responsible for evolution.

**7. Comprehensive Testing**  
Shared kernels require exhaustive test coverage due to wide usage.

### 163.4 Platform Shared Kernel Map

        SM[State Machine Kernel]
        CF[Custom Field Kernel]

# **PART XVII - CUSTOM FIELD KERNEL**

## **Chapter 164 - Custom Field Kernel Overview**

### 164.1 Purpose and Scope

The Custom Field Kernel provides **universal dynamic schema extension** capabilities, enabling:

- User-defined attributes without database migrations
- Type-safe value storage and validation
- Conditional visibility and requirement rules
- Field-level permissions
- Versioning and change tracking
- Rich field types (text, number, date, lookup, etc.)

**Used By:**
- Task Instance (task custom fields)
- Task Type (type-specific fields)
- Project (project attributes)
- Approval Workflow (request metadata)
- Workflow (transition data capture)
- Case (case-specific attributes)

### 164.2 Core Value Proposition

**Before Custom Fields:**
```sql
-- Schema change required for new attribute
ALTER TABLE Tasks ADD COLUMN EstimatedCost DECIMAL(10,2);
-- Requires deployment, migration, downtime
```

**With Custom Fields:**
```json
{
  "fieldDefinition": {
    "name": "Estimated Cost",
    "type": "Currency",
    "required": false,
    "defaultValue": 0
  }
}
// No schema change, instant availability
```

### 165.3 Validation Engine

```csharp
public class CustomFieldValidator
{
    public ValidationResult Validate(
        CustomFieldDefinition definition,
        object value)
    {
        var result = new ValidationResult();
        
        // Null check for required fields
        if (definition.IsRequired && value == null)
        {
            result.AddError($"{definition.Name} is required");
            return result;
        }
        
        if (value == null)
            return result; // Optional field, null is valid
        
        // Type-specific validation
        switch (definition.Type)
        {
            case CustomFieldType.Text:
                ValidateText(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            case CustomFieldType.Number:
                ValidateNumber(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            case CustomFieldType.Date:
                ValidateDate(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            case CustomFieldType.Select:
                ValidateSelect(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            case CustomFieldType.User:
                ValidateUserReference(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            case CustomFieldType.File:
                ValidateFile(value, definition.ValidationRules, result);
                break;
                
            // ... other types
        }
        
        return result;
    }
    
    private void ValidateText(
        object value,
        Json rules,
        ValidationResult result)
    {
        var text = value.ToString();
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("minLength"))
        {
            var min = rules["minLength"].ToObject<int>();
            if (text.Length < min)
                result.AddError($"Minimum length is {min} characters");
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("maxLength"))
        {
            var max = rules["maxLength"].ToObject<int>();
            if (text.Length > max)
                result.AddError($"Maximum length is {max} characters");
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("pattern"))
        {
            var pattern = rules["pattern"].ToString();
            if (!Regex.IsMatch(text, pattern))
                result.AddError($"Value does not match required pattern");
        }
    }
    
    private void ValidateNumber(
        object value,
        Json rules,
        ValidationResult result)
    {
        if (!decimal.TryParse(value.ToString(), out var number))
        {
            result.AddError("Value must be a number");
            return;
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("min"))
        {
            var min = rules["min"].ToObject<decimal>();
            if (number < min)
                result.AddError($"Value must be at least {min}");
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("max"))
        {
            var max = rules["max"].ToObject<decimal>();
            if (number > max)
                result.AddError($"Value must be at most {max}");
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("allowDecimals") && 
            !rules["allowDecimals"].ToObject<bool>())
        {
            if (number % 1 != 0)
                result.AddError("Decimal values are not allowed");
        }
    }
    
    private async Task ValidateUserReference(
        object value,
        Json rules,
        ValidationResult result)
    {
        if (!Guid.TryParse(value.ToString(), out var userId))
        {
            result.AddError("Invalid user reference");
            return;
        }
        
        var user = await _userRepository.GetAsync(userId);
        if (user == null)
        {
            result.AddError("User not found");
            return;
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("mustBeActive") && 
            rules["mustBeActive"].ToObject<bool>())
        {
            if (!user.IsActive)
                result.AddError("User must be active");
        }
        
        if (rules.ContainsKey("allowedRoles"))
        {
            var allowedRoles = rules["allowedRoles"].ToObject<List<string>>();
            if (!user.Roles.Any(r => allowedRoles.Contains(r)))
                result.AddError($"User must have one of: {string.Join(", ", allowedRoles)}");
        }
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 166 - Conditional Visibility & Requirements**

### 166.1 Visibility Rules

**Purpose:** Control when fields are displayed based on context.

```json
{
  "fieldDefinition": {
    "name": "Deployment Environment",
    "type": "Select",
    "visibilityRules": [
      {
        "condition": {
          "field": "TaskType",
          "operator": "equals",
          "value": "Deployment"
        },
        "visible": true
      },
      {
        "condition": {
          "field": "Status",
          "operator": "in",
          "value": ["In Progress", "Ready for Deploy"]
        },
        "visible": true
      }
    ],
    "defaultVisibility": false
  }
}
```

**Evaluation Engine:**
```csharp
public class VisibilityRuleEvaluator
{
    public bool IsVisible(
        CustomFieldDefinition field,
        Dictionary<string, object> context)
    {
        if (field.VisibilityRules == null || !field.VisibilityRules.Any())
            return field.DefaultVisibility;
        
        foreach (var rule in field.VisibilityRules)
        {
            if (EvaluateCondition(rule.Condition, context))
                return rule.Visible;
        }
        
        return field.DefaultVisibility;
    }
    
    private bool EvaluateCondition(
        VisibilityCondition condition,
        Dictionary<string, object> context)
    {
        if (!context.TryGetValue(condition.Field, out var actualValue))
            return false;
        
        return condition.Operator switch
        {
            "equals" => Equals(actualValue, condition.Value),
            "notEquals" => !Equals(actualValue, condition.Value),
            "in" => condition.Value is IList list && list.Contains(actualValue),
            "notIn" => condition.Value is IList list2 && !list2.Contains(actualValue),
            "greaterThan" => Compare(actualValue, condition.Value) > 0,
            "lessThan" => Compare(actualValue, condition.Value) < 0,
            "contains" => actualValue.ToString().Contains(condition.Value.ToString()),
            _ => false
        };
    }
}
```

        TeamMembers
        RoleBased
        UserSpecific
        Owner
        Admin
    }
    
    CustomFieldPermission "1" --> "1" PermissionLevel

### 167.3 Permission Enforcement

```csharp
public class CustomFieldPermissionService
{
    public async Task<bool> CanReadFieldAsync(
        Guid userId,
        CustomFieldDefinition field)
    {
        var userContext = await _userContextService.GetAsync(userId);
        
        return field.Permissions.ReadLevel switch
        {
            PermissionLevel.Public => true,
            
            PermissionLevel.Internal => userContext.TenantId == field.TenantId,
            
            PermissionLevel.RoleBased => 
                userContext.Roles.Any(r => 
                    field.Permissions.AllowedRoles.Contains(r)),
            
            PermissionLevel.TeamMembers =>
                userContext.Teams.Any(t =>
                    field.Permissions.AllowedTeams.Contains(t)),
            
            PermissionLevel.UserSpecific =>
                field.Permissions.AllowedUsers.Contains(userId),
            
            PermissionLevel.Admin =>
                userContext.IsAdmin,
            
            _ => false
        };
    }
    
    public async Task<bool> CanWriteFieldAsync(
        Guid userId,
        CustomFieldDefinition field,
        Guid entityId)
    {
        if (!await CanReadFieldAsync(userId, field))
            return false; // Cannot write if cannot read
        
        var userContext = await _userContextService.GetAsync(userId);
        
        return field.Permissions.WriteLevel switch
        {
            PermissionLevel.Owner => await IsOwnerAsync(userId, entityId),
            
            PermissionLevel.RoleBased =>
                userContext.Roles.Any(r =>
                    field.Permissions.AllowedRoles.Contains(r)),
            
            PermissionLevel.Admin => userContext.IsAdmin,
            
            _ => false
        };
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 168 - Custom Field Storage**

### 168.1 Storage Strategies

**Option 1: JSON Column (Recommended)**
```sql
CREATE TABLE Tasks (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    Title VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    -- ... other columns
    CustomFields JSONB,
    CONSTRAINT valid_custom_fields CHECK (
        jsonb_typeof(CustomFields) = 'object'
    )
);

-- Index for efficient querying
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_custom_fields 
ON Tasks USING GIN (CustomFields);

-- Query example
SELECT * FROM Tasks
WHERE CustomFields->>'priority' = 'High'
  AND (CustomFields->>'estimated_cost')::decimal > 10000;
```

**Option 2: EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) Pattern**
```sql
CREATE TABLE CustomFieldValues (
    Id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    EntityId UUID NOT NULL,
    EntityType VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    FieldDefinitionId UUID NOT NULL,
    ValueText TEXT,
    ValueNumber DECIMAL(18,4),
    ValueDate TIMESTAMP,
    ValueBoolean BOOLEAN,
    ValueJson JSONB,
    CreatedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
    FOREIGN KEY (FieldDefinitionId) 
        REFERENCES CustomFieldDefinitions(Id)
);

-- Composite index for efficient lookups
CREATE INDEX idx_cfv_entity 
ON CustomFieldValues(EntityId, EntityType, FieldDefinitionId);
```

**Option 3: Hybrid Approach**
- Frequently queried fields → dedicated columns
- Rarely queried fields → JSON column
- Large text/binary → separate table with references

### 168.2 Query Performance

**Optimization Techniques:**

1. **JSON Path Indexes:**
```sql
-- Create index on specific JSON path
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_cf_priority 
ON Tasks ((CustomFields->>'priority'));

CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_cf_cost
ON Tasks (((CustomFields->>'estimated_cost')::decimal));
```

2. **Materialized Views:**
```sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW TasksWithPriority AS
SELECT 
    Id,
    Title,
    CustomFields->>'priority' as Priority,
    (CustomFields->>'estimated_cost')::decimal as EstimatedCost
FROM Tasks
WHERE CustomFields IS NOT NULL;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON TasksWithPriority(Id);
```

3. **Computed Columns:**
```sql
ALTER TABLE Tasks 
ADD COLUMN Priority VARCHAR(50) 
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CustomFields->>'priority') STORED;

CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_priority ON Tasks(Priority);
```

## **Chapter 169 - Custom Field Versioning**

### 169.1 Version Model

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class CustomFieldDefinition {
        +Guid Id
        +int Version
        +DateTime CreatedAt
        +DateTime? DeprecatedAt
    }
    
    class CustomFieldVersion {
        +Guid DefinitionId
        +int VersionNumber
        +string Name
        +CustomFieldType Type
        +Json ValidationRules
        +bool IsActive
        +DateTime CreatedAt
        +string ChangeDescription
    }
    
    CustomFieldDefinition "1" --> "*" CustomFieldVersion
```

### 169.2 Breaking vs Non-Breaking Changes

**Non-Breaking Changes (Minor Version):**
- Adding new validation rule (more permissive)
- Updating display configuration
- Changing field description
- Adding new allowed values to select
- Increasing max length
- Making required field optional

**Breaking Changes (Major Version):**
- Changing field type
- Removing allowed values from select
- Making optional field required
- Decreasing max length
- Adding stricter validation rules
- Changing field key/name

### 169.3 Migration Strategy

```csharp
public class CustomFieldMigrationService
{
    public async Task MigrateFieldAsync(
        CustomFieldDefinition field,
        CustomFieldDefinition newVersion)
    {
        // Validate migration is safe
        var validation = ValidateMigration(field, newVersion);
        if (!validation.IsValid)
            throw new InvalidMigrationException(validation.Errors);
        
        // Create new version
        var version = field.CreateVersion(newVersion);
        await _repository.SaveVersionAsync(version);
        
        // Migrate existing values if needed
        if (RequiresDataMigration(field, newVersion))
        {
            await MigrateExistingValuesAsync(field, newVersion);
        }
        
        // Deprecate old version
        field.Deprecate();
        await _repository.UpdateAsync(field);
    }
    
    private async Task MigrateExistingValuesAsync(
        CustomFieldDefinition oldField,
        CustomFieldDefinition newField)
    {
        // Example: Migrating from Text to Select
        if (oldField.Type == CustomFieldType.Text &&
            newField.Type == CustomFieldType.Select)
        {
            var entities = await _entityRepo.GetWithFieldAsync(oldField.Id);
            
            foreach (var entity in entities)
            {
                var oldValue = entity.GetCustomFieldValue(oldField.Key);
                var newValue = MapTextToSelectValue(
                    oldValue,
                    newField.ValidationRules["allowedValues"]);
                
                entity.SetCustomFieldValue(newField.Key, newValue);
                await _entityRepo.UpdateAsync(entity);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

public class CustomFieldTemplateService
{
    public async Task ApplyTemplateAsync(
        Guid entityId,
        string templateId)
    {
        var template = await _templateRepo.GetAsync(templateId);
        
        foreach (var fieldDef in template.Fields)
        {
            // Check if field already exists
            var existing = await _fieldRepo.FindByKeyAsync(
                entityId,
                fieldDef.Key);
            
            if (existing != null)
            {
                // Skip or update based on strategy
                continue;
            }
            
            // Create field definition
            var field = new CustomFieldDefinition
            {
                TenantId = _currentTenant.Id,
                Name = fieldDef.Name,
                Key = fieldDef.Key,
                Type = fieldDef.Type,
                IsRequired = fieldDef.Required,
                ValidationRules = fieldDef.ValidationRules,
                DisplayConfig = fieldDef.DisplayConfig,
                ApplicableContexts = new[] { entityId.ToString() }
            };
            
            await _fieldRepo.InsertAsync(field);
        }
    }
}

## **Chapter 171 - Custom Field Performance**

### 171.1 Caching Strategy

```csharp
public class CustomFieldCacheService
{
    private readonly IDistributedCache _cache;
    private readonly TimeSpan _cacheDuration = TimeSpan.FromHours(4);
    
    public async Task<List<CustomFieldDefinition>> GetFieldsForEntityAsync(
        string entityType)
    {
        var cacheKey = $"custom_fields:{entityType}";
        
        var cached = await _cache.GetAsync<List<CustomFieldDefinition>>(cacheKey);
        if (cached != null)
            return cached;
        
        var fields = await _repository.GetByEntityTypeAsync(entityType);
        
        await _cache.SetAsync(
            cacheKey,
            fields,
            new DistributedCacheEntryOptions
            {
                AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = _cacheDuration
            });
        
        return fields;
    }
    
    public async Task InvalidateCacheAsync(string entityType)
    {
        await _cache.RemoveAsync($"custom_fields:{entityType}");
    }
}
```

### 171.2 Batch Value Operations

```csharp
public class CustomFieldBatchService
{
    public async Task SetValuesAsync(
        Guid entityId,
        Dictionary<string, object> values)
    {
        // Load all field definitions at once
        var fieldKeys = values.Keys.ToList();
        var definitions = await _fieldRepo.GetByKeysAsync(fieldKeys);
        
        // Validate all values
        var validationErrors = new List<ValidationError>();
        var validatedValues = new Dictionary<string, object>();
        
        foreach (var kvp in values)
        {
            var definition = definitions.FirstOrDefault(d => d.Key == kvp.Key);
            if (definition == null)
            {
                validationErrors.Add(new ValidationError(
                    kvp.Key,
                    "Field definition not found"));
                continue;
            }
            
            var validation = _validator.Validate(definition, kvp.Value);
            if (!validation.IsValid)
            {
                validationErrors.AddRange(validation.Errors);
                continue;
            }
            
            validatedValues[kvp.Key] = kvp.Value;
        }
        
        if (validationErrors.Any())
            throw new ValidationException(validationErrors);
        
        // Bulk update
        await _valueRepo.SetManyAsync(entityId, validatedValues);
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 173 - Dependency Kernel Overview**

### 173.1 Purpose and Scope

The Dependency Kernel provides **universal dependency management and graph analysis** capabilities, enabling:

- Dependency relationship modeling
- Circular dependency detection
- Topological sorting
- Critical path calculation
- Earliest/latest start date computation
- Slack time analysis
- Dependency type support (FS, SS, FF, SF)
- Lag and lead time modeling
- Dependency impact analysis

**Used By:**
- Project Context (project-to-project dependencies)
- Task Instance Context (task-to-task dependencies)
- Case Context (milestone dependencies)
- Resource Context (resource dependencies)

### 173.2 Core Value Proposition

**Problem Without Dependency Kernel:**
- Duplicated dependency logic across contexts
- Inconsistent circular detection algorithms
- Different critical path calculations
- Hard to maintain graph algorithms
- No unified dependency queries

**Solution With Dependency Kernel:**
- Single source of truth for dependency logic
- Proven, tested graph algorithms
- Consistent behavior across all contexts
- Reusable graph analysis services
- Unified dependency query language

### 173.3 Dependency Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Consumers ["Consumer Contexts"]
        Project[Project Context]
        Task[Task Instance Context]
        Case[Case Context]
    end
    
    subgraph DependencyKernel ["Dependency Kernel"]
        Graph[Dependency Graph]
        Validator[Circular Detector]
        Analyzer[Critical Path Analyzer]
        Calculator[Date Calculator]
        Sorter[Topological Sorter]
    end
    
    subgraph Algorithms ["Core Algorithms"]
        DFS[Depth-First Search]
        Bellman[Bellman-Ford]
        Kahn[Kahn's Algorithm]
        Floyd[Floyd-Warshall]
    end
    
    Project --> Graph
    Task --> Graph
    Case --> Graph
    
    Graph --> Validator
    Graph --> Analyzer
    Graph --> Calculator
    Graph --> Sorter
    
    Validator --> DFS
    Analyzer --> Bellman
    Sorter --> Kahn
    Calculator --> Floyd
```

## **Chapter 175 - Circular Dependency Detection**

### 175.1 Detection Algorithm

**Depth-First Search (DFS) Based Detection:**

```csharp
public class CircularDependencyDetector
{
    private enum VisitState { Unvisited, Visiting, Visited }
    
    public CircularDependencyResult DetectCycle(DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var visitState = new Dictionary<Guid, VisitState>();
        var parent = new Dictionary<Guid, Guid>();
        
        // Initialize all nodes as unvisited
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            visitState[node.Id] = VisitState.Unvisited;
        }
        
        // DFS from each unvisited node
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            if (visitState[node.Id] == VisitState.Unvisited)
            {
                var cycle = DFS(node, visitState, parent, graph);
                if (cycle != null)
                {
                    return new CircularDependencyResult
                    {
                        HasCycle = true,
                        CyclePath = cycle,
                        Message = BuildCycleMessage(cycle, graph)
                    };
                }
            }
        }
        
        return new CircularDependencyResult
        {
            HasCycle = false
        };
    }
    
    private List<Guid> DFS(
        DependencyNode node,
        Dictionary<Guid, VisitState> visitState,
        Dictionary<Guid, Guid> parent,
        DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        visitState[node.Id] = VisitState.Visiting;
        
        foreach (var edge in node.OutgoingEdges)
        {
            var neighbor = graph.GetNode(edge.ToNodeId);
            
            if (visitState[neighbor.Id] == VisitState.Visiting)
            {
                // Cycle detected - reconstruct path
                return ReconstructCycle(node.Id, neighbor.Id, parent);
            }
            
            if (visitState[neighbor.Id] == VisitState.Unvisited)
            {
                parent[neighbor.Id] = node.Id;
                var cycle = DFS(neighbor, visitState, parent, graph);
                if (cycle != null)
                    return cycle;
            }
        }
        
        visitState[node.Id] = VisitState.Visited;
        return null;
    }
    
    private List<Guid> ReconstructCycle(
        Guid currentId,
        Guid cycleStartId,
        Dictionary<Guid, Guid> parent)
    {
        var cycle = new List<Guid> { cycleStartId };
        var current = currentId;
        
        while (current != cycleStartId)
        {
            cycle.Insert(0, current);
            current = parent[current];
        }
        
        cycle.Add(cycleStartId); // Complete the cycle
        return cycle;
    }
    
    private string BuildCycleMessage(List<Guid> cycle, DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var nodeNames = cycle.Select(id => 
            graph.GetNode(id)?.EntityId.ToString() ?? "Unknown").ToList();
        
        return $"Circular dependency detected: {string.Join(" → ", nodeNames)}";
    }
}
```

### 175.2 Validation at Add Time

```csharp
public class DependencyGraphService
{
    public async Task<AddDependencyResult> AddDependencyAsync(
        DependencyGraph graph,
        DependencyEdge newEdge)
    {
        // Temporarily add edge
        graph.AddEdge(newEdge);
        
        // Check for cycles
        var cycleCheck = _circularDetector.DetectCycle(graph);
        
        if (cycleCheck.HasCycle)
        {
            // Remove the edge
            graph.RemoveEdge(newEdge.Id);
            
            return new AddDependencyResult
            {
                Success = false,
                Error = "Cannot add dependency - would create circular dependency",
                CyclePath = cycleCheck.CyclePath
            };
        }
        
        // Persist the change
        await _repository.SaveGraphAsync(graph);
        
        return new AddDependencyResult
        {
            Success = true,
            EdgeId = newEdge.Id
        };
    }
}
```

### 175.3 User-Friendly Error Messages

```csharp
public class CycleMessageBuilder
{
    public string BuildUserMessage(
        List<Guid> cyclePath,
        DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var nodes = cyclePath.Select(id => graph.GetNode(id)).ToList();
        
        var message = new StringBuilder();
        message.AppendLine("❌ Cannot create dependency - circular reference detected:");
        message.AppendLine();
        
        for (int i = 0; i < nodes.Count - 1; i++)
        {
            var from = nodes[i];
            var to = nodes[i + 1];
            var edge = graph.GetEdge(from.Id, to.Id);
            
            message.AppendLine($"  {i + 1}. {GetNodeDescription(from)}");
            message.AppendLine($"     ↓ {GetEdgeDescription(edge)}");
        }
        
        message.AppendLine($"  {nodes.Count}. {GetNodeDescription(nodes.Last())}");
        message.AppendLine();
        message.AppendLine("💡 To fix: Remove one of the dependencies in this chain.");
        
        return message.ToString();
    }
    
    private string GetNodeDescription(DependencyNode node)
    {
        return node.EntityType switch
        {
            "Task" => $"Task: {GetTaskTitle(node.EntityId)}",
            "Project" => $"Project: {GetProjectTitle(node.EntityId)}",
            _ => $"{node.EntityType} {node.EntityId}"
        };
    }
    
    private string GetEdgeDescription(DependencyEdge edge)
    {
        var type = edge.Type.ToString();
        var lag = edge.Lag != Duration.Zero 
            ? $" (lag: {edge.Lag})" 
            : "";
        return $"{type}{lag}";
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 176 - Topological Sorting**

### 176.1 Purpose

Topological sorting provides a linear ordering of nodes such that for every edge (u, v), node u comes before node v. This is essential for:

- Determining execution order
- Scheduling tasks
- Identifying what can be done in parallel
- Validating dependency consistency

### 176.2 Kahn's Algorithm Implementation

```csharp
public class TopologicalSorter
{
    public TopologicalSortResult Sort(DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        // Step 1: Calculate in-degree for each node
        var inDegree = new Dictionary<Guid, int>();
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            inDegree[node.Id] = node.IncomingEdges.Count;
        }
        
        // Step 2: Queue nodes with zero in-degree
        var queue = new Queue<Guid>();
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            if (inDegree[node.Id] == 0)
                queue.Enqueue(node.Id);
        }
        
        // Step 3: Process queue
        var sorted = new List<Guid>();
        var levels = new Dictionary<Guid, int>(); // For parallel execution hints
        
        while (queue.Any())
        {
            // All nodes at current queue position can execute in parallel
            var currentLevel = new List<Guid>();
            var levelSize = queue.Count;
            
            for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++)
            {
                var nodeId = queue.Dequeue();
                sorted.Add(nodeId);
                currentLevel.Add(nodeId);
                
                var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
                
                // Reduce in-degree for neighbors
                foreach (var edge in node.OutgoingEdges)
                {
                    inDegree[edge.ToNodeId]--;
                    
                    if (inDegree[edge.ToNodeId] == 0)
                        queue.Enqueue(edge.ToNodeId);
                }
            }
            
            // Record level for parallel execution
            foreach (var nodeId in currentLevel)
            {
                levels[nodeId] = sorted.Count / levelSize;
            }
        }
        
        // Step 4: Check if all nodes were processed
        if (sorted.Count != graph.Nodes.Count)
        {
            return new TopologicalSortResult
            {
                Success = false,
                Error = "Graph contains a cycle - topological sort impossible",
                PartialOrder = sorted
            };
        }
        
        return new TopologicalSortResult
        {
            Success = true,
            Order = sorted,
            Levels = levels,
            ParallelizationGroups = GroupByLevel(sorted, levels)
        };
    }
    
    private List<List<Guid>> GroupByLevel(
        List<Guid> sorted,
        Dictionary<Guid, int> levels)
    {
        var groups = new List<List<Guid>>();
        
        foreach (var nodeId in sorted)
        {
            var level = levels[nodeId];
            
            while (groups.Count <= level)
                groups.Add(new List<Guid>());
            
            groups[level].Add(nodeId);
        }
        
        return groups;
    }
}
```

### 176.3 Parallelization Hints

```csharp
public class ParallelExecutionPlanner
{
    public ExecutionPlan CreatePlan(TopologicalSortResult sortResult)
    {
        var plan = new ExecutionPlan();
        
        foreach (var group in sortResult.ParallelizationGroups)
        {
            plan.Phases.Add(new ExecutionPhase
            {
                PhaseNumber = plan.Phases.Count + 1,
                ParallelTasks = group,
                CanExecuteInParallel = true,
                Description = $"Phase {plan.Phases.Count + 1}: " +
                             $"{group.Count} tasks can run concurrently"
            });
        }
        
        return plan;
    }
}

## **Chapter 177 - Critical Path Analysis**

### 177.1 Critical Path Method (CPM)

The **Critical Path** is the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the minimum project duration.

**Key Concepts:**
- **ES (Earliest Start):** Earliest time an activity can start
- **EF (Earliest Finish):** Earliest time an activity can finish
- **LS (Latest Start):** Latest time an activity can start without delaying project
- **LF (Latest Finish):** Latest time an activity can finish without delaying project
- **Slack/Float:** LS - ES (or LF - EF) - how much delay is tolerable

### 177.2 Forward Pass (Calculate ES and EF)

```csharp
public class CriticalPathAnalyzer
{
    public CriticalPathResult Analyze(DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var nodes = graph.Nodes.ToDictionary(n => n.Id, n => n);
        var calculations = new Dictionary<Guid, NodeCalculation>();
        
        // Initialize calculations
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            calculations[node.Id] = new NodeCalculation
            {
                NodeId = node.Id,
                Duration = node.EstimatedDuration
            };
        }
        
        // Forward Pass: Calculate ES and EF
        var sorted = TopologicalSort(graph);
        
        foreach (var nodeId in sorted)
        {
            var node = nodes[nodeId];
            var calc = calculations[nodeId];
            
            if (node.IncomingEdges.Count == 0)
            {
                // No predecessors - can start immediately
                calc.EarliestStart = TimeSpan.Zero;
            }
            else
            {
                // ES = max(predecessor EF + lag)
                calc.EarliestStart = node.IncomingEdges
                    .Select(edge => 
                    {
                        var predCalc = calculations[edge.FromNodeId];
                        return CalculateDependencyTime(
                            predCalc,
                            edge,
                            isForward: true);
                    })
                    .Max();
            }
            
            calc.EarliestFinish = calc.EarliestStart + calc.Duration;
        }
        
        // Backward Pass: Calculate LS and LF
        var projectDuration = calculations.Values.Max(c => c.EarliestFinish);
        
        foreach (var nodeId in sorted.Reverse<Guid>())
        {
            var node = nodes[nodeId];
            var calc = calculations[nodeId];
            
            if (node.OutgoingEdges.Count == 0)
            {
                // No successors - must finish by project end
                calc.LatestFinish = projectDuration;
            }
            else
            {
                // LF = min(successor LS - lag)
                calc.LatestFinish = node.OutgoingEdges
                    .Select(edge =>
                    {
                        var succCalc = calculations[edge.ToNodeId];
                        return CalculateDependencyTime(
                            succCalc,
                            edge,
                            isForward: false);
                    })
                    .Min();
            }
            
            calc.LatestStart = calc.LatestFinish - calc.Duration;
            calc.TotalSlack = calc.LatestStart - calc.EarliestStart;
            calc.IsCritical = calc.TotalSlack == TimeSpan.Zero;
        }
        
        // Identify critical path
        var criticalPath = FindCriticalPath(graph, calculations);
        
        return new CriticalPathResult
        {
            ProjectDuration = projectDuration,
            CriticalPath = criticalPath,
            Calculations = calculations,
            CriticalPathLength = criticalPath.Count
        };
    }
    
    private TimeSpan CalculateDependencyTime(
        NodeCalculation calculation,
        DependencyEdge edge,
        bool isForward)
    {
        return edge.Type switch
        {
            DependencyType.FinishToStart => 
                isForward 
                    ? calculation.EarliestFinish + edge.Lag
                    : calculation.LatestStart - edge.Lag,
            
            DependencyType.StartToStart =>
                isForward
                    ? calculation.EarliestStart + edge.Lag
                    : calculation.LatestStart - edge.Lag,
            
            DependencyType.FinishToFinish =>
                isForward
                    ? calculation.EarliestFinish + edge.Lag - calculation.Duration
                    : calculation.LatestFinish - edge.Lag,
            
            DependencyType.StartToFinish =>
                isForward
                    ? calculation.EarliestStart + edge.Lag - calculation.Duration
                    : calculation.LatestFinish - edge.Lag,
            
            _ => TimeSpan.Zero
        };
    }
    
    private List<Guid> FindCriticalPath(
        DependencyGraph graph,
        Dictionary<Guid, NodeCalculation> calculations)
    {
        var criticalNodes = calculations
            .Where(kvp => kvp.Value.IsCritical)
            .Select(kvp => kvp.Key)
            .ToList();
        
        // Build path by following critical edges
        var path = new List<Guid>();
        var visited = new HashSet<Guid>();
        
        // Find starting critical node (no predecessors or earliest start = 0)
        var start = criticalNodes
            .Where(id => calculations[id].EarliestStart == TimeSpan.Zero)
            .FirstOrDefault();
        
        if (start != Guid.Empty)
        {
            BuildCriticalPath(start, graph, calculations, path, visited);
        }
        
        return path;
    }
    
    private void BuildCriticalPath(
        Guid nodeId,
        DependencyGraph graph,
        Dictionary<Guid, NodeCalculation> calculations,
        List<Guid> path,
        HashSet<Guid> visited)
    {
        if (visited.Contains(nodeId))
            return;
        
        visited.Add(nodeId);
        path.Add(nodeId);
        
        var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
        
        // Find next critical node
        var nextCritical = node.OutgoingEdges
            .Select(edge => edge.ToNodeId)
            .FirstOrDefault(id => 
                calculations[id].IsCritical && 
                !visited.Contains(id));
        
        if (nextCritical != Guid.Empty)
        {
            BuildCriticalPath(nextCritical, graph, calculations, path, visited);
        }
    }
}
```

        var nonCritical = result.Calculations
            .Where(kvp => !kvp.Value.IsCritical)
            .OrderBy(kvp => kvp.Value.TotalSlack)

        }
        
        return sb.ToString();
    }
}

## **Chapter 178 - Date Calculation Service**

### 178.1 Earliest Start Date Calculator

```csharp
public class DependencyDateCalculator
{
    private readonly IWorkingCalendarService _calendarService;
    
    public async Task<DateTime> CalculateEarliestStartAsync(
        DependencyNode node,
        DependencyGraph graph,
        Guid calendarId)
    {
        var calendar = await _calendarService.GetAsync(calendarId);
        
        // If no dependencies, can start immediately
        if (!node.IncomingEdges.Any())
        {
            return node.PlannedStart ?? DateTime.UtcNow;
        }
        
        // Calculate based on predecessor completion
        var earliestStart = DateTime.MinValue;
        
        foreach (var edge in node.IncomingEdges)
        {
            var predecessor = graph.GetNode(edge.FromNodeId);
            
            var dependencyDate = edge.Type switch
            {
                DependencyType.FinishToStart => 
                    await CalculateFinishToStartAsync(
                        predecessor, edge, calendar),
                
                DependencyType.StartToStart =>
                    await CalculateStartToStartAsync(
                        predecessor, edge, calendar),
                
                DependencyType.FinishToFinish =>
                    await CalculateFinishToFinishAsync(
                        predecessor, node, edge, calendar),
                
                DependencyType.StartToFinish =>
                    await CalculateStartToFinishAsync(
                        predecessor, node, edge, calendar),
                
                _ => DateTime.MaxValue
            };
            
            if (dependencyDate > earliestStart)
                earliestStart = dependencyDate;
        }
        
        return earliestStart;
    }
    
    private async Task<DateTime> CalculateFinishToStartAsync(
        DependencyNode predecessor,
        DependencyEdge edge,
        WorkingCalendar calendar)
    {
        // Successor starts after predecessor finishes (+ lag)
        var predecessorEnd = predecessor.PlannedEnd 
            ?? await EstimateEndDateAsync(predecessor, calendar);
        
        if (edge.Lag != Duration.Zero)
        {
            return await calendar.AddBusinessTimeAsync(
                predecessorEnd,
                edge.Lag);
        }
        
        return predecessorEnd;
    }
    
    private async Task<DateTime> CalculateStartToStartAsync(
        DependencyNode predecessor,
        DependencyEdge edge,
        WorkingCalendar calendar)
    {
        // Successor starts when predecessor starts (+ lag)
        var predecessorStart = predecessor.PlannedStart 
            ?? predecessor.ActualStart 
            ?? DateTime.UtcNow;
        
        if (edge.Lag != Duration.Zero)
        {
            return await calendar.AddBusinessTimeAsync(
                predecessorStart,
                edge.Lag);
        }
        
        return predecessorStart;
    }
    
    private async Task<DateTime> CalculateFinishToFinishAsync(
        DependencyNode predecessor,
        DependencyNode successor,
        DependencyEdge edge,
        WorkingCalendar calendar)
    {
        // Successor finishes when predecessor finishes (+ lag)
        // Work backward from finish to find start
        var predecessorEnd = predecessor.PlannedEnd 
            ?? await EstimateEndDateAsync(predecessor, calendar);
        
        var successorEnd = edge.Lag != Duration.Zero
            ? await calendar.AddBusinessTimeAsync(predecessorEnd, edge.Lag)
            : predecessorEnd;
        
        // Calculate start from finish
        return await calendar.SubtractBusinessTimeAsync(
            successorEnd,
            successor.EstimatedDuration);
    }
    
    private async Task<DateTime> EstimateEndDateAsync(
        DependencyNode node,
        WorkingCalendar calendar)
    {
        var start = node.PlannedStart 
            ?? node.ActualStart 
            ?? DateTime.UtcNow;
        
        return await calendar.AddBusinessTimeAsync(
            start,
            node.EstimatedDuration);
    }
}
```

### 178.2 Impact Analysis

**Purpose:** Determine how changes to one task affect dependent tasks.

```csharp
public class DependencyImpactAnalyzer
{
    public async Task<ImpactAnalysisResult> AnalyzeDelayImpactAsync(
        Guid nodeId,
        Duration additionalDelay,
        DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var result = new ImpactAnalysisResult
        {
            OriginNodeId = nodeId,
            Delay = additionalDelay,
            ImpactedNodes = new List<NodeImpact>()
        };
        
        // Get critical path analysis
        var criticalPath = await _criticalPathAnalyzer.Analyze(graph);
        
        var originNode = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
        var originCalc = criticalPath.Calculations[nodeId];
        
        // If node is not on critical path and has slack, delay may not propagate
        if (!originCalc.IsCritical && 
            originCalc.TotalSlack >= additionalDelay)
        {
            result.ProjectDelayed = false;
            result.Message = "Delay absorbed by slack time - no project impact";
            return result;
        }
        
        // Find all downstream dependencies
        var impacted = await FindImpactedNodesAsync(
            nodeId,
            additionalDelay,
            graph,
            criticalPath);
        
        result.ImpactedNodes = impacted;
        result.ProjectDelayed = impacted.Any(i => i.DelayAmount > TimeSpan.Zero);
        result.TotalProjectDelay = impacted.Max(i => i.DelayAmount);
        
        return result;
    }
    
    private async Task<List<NodeImpact>> FindImpactedNodesAsync(
        Guid originId,
        Duration delay,
        DependencyGraph graph,
        CriticalPathResult criticalPath)
    {
        var impacted = new List<NodeImpact>();
        var visited = new HashSet<Guid>();
        var queue = new Queue<(Guid nodeId, Duration cumulativeDelay)>();
        
        queue.Enqueue((originId, delay));
        
        while (queue.Any())
        {
            var (nodeId, currentDelay) = queue.Dequeue();
            
            if (visited.Contains(nodeId))
                continue;
            
            visited.Add(nodeId);
            
            var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
            var calc = criticalPath.Calculations[nodeId];
            
            // Calculate actual impact considering slack
            var actualDelay = currentDelay > calc.TotalSlack
                ? currentDelay - calc.TotalSlack
                : TimeSpan.Zero;
            
            if (actualDelay > TimeSpan.Zero)
            {
                impacted.Add(new NodeImpact
                {
                    NodeId = nodeId,
                    NodeName = GetNodeName(node),
                    OriginalStart = calc.EarliestStart,
                    NewStart = calc.EarliestStart + actualDelay,
                    DelayAmount = actualDelay,
                    IsCritical = calc.IsCritical,
                    AvailableSlack = calc.TotalSlack
                });
                
                // Propagate to successors
                foreach (var edge in node.OutgoingEdges)
                {
                    queue.Enqueue((edge.ToNodeId, actualDelay));
                }
            }
        }
        
        return impacted;
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 179 - Dependency Constraints & Blocking**

### 179.1 Blocking Dependencies

```csharp
public class DependencyConstraintService
{
    public async Task<bool> CanStartAsync(
        Guid nodeId,
        DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
        
        // Check all incoming dependencies
        foreach (var edge in node.IncomingEdges)
        {
            if (!edge.IsBlocking)
                continue; // Optional dependency
            
            var predecessor = graph.GetNode(edge.FromNodeId);
            
            // Check if predecessor constraint is satisfied
            var satisfied = edge.Type switch
            {
                DependencyType.FinishToStart => 
                    predecessor.IsComplete(),
                
                DependencyType.StartToStart =>
                    predecessor.ActualStart.HasValue,
                
                DependencyType.FinishToFinish =>
                    true, // FF doesn't block start
                
                DependencyType.StartToFinish =>
                    true, // SF doesn't block start
                
                _ => false
            };
            
            if (!satisfied)
            {
                return false;
            }
        }
        
        return true;
    }
    
    public async Task<List<BlockingDependency>> GetBlockingDependenciesAsync(
        Guid nodeId,
        DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var blockers = new List<BlockingDependency>();
        var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
        
        foreach (var edge in node.IncomingEdges.Where(e => e.IsBlocking))
        {
            if (!await IsSatisfiedAsync(edge, graph))
            {
                var predecessor = graph.GetNode(edge.FromNodeId);
                
                blockers.Add(new BlockingDependency
                {
                    EdgeId = edge.Id,
                    PredecessorId = predecessor.Id,
                    PredecessorName = GetNodeName(predecessor),
                    Type = edge.Type,
                    Reason = GetBlockingReason(edge, predecessor),
                    EstimatedResolutionDate = await EstimateResolutionAsync(
                        predecessor,
                        edge)
                });
            }
        }
        
        return blockers;
    }
    
    private string GetBlockingReason(
        DependencyEdge edge,
        DependencyNode predecessor)
    {
        return edge.Type switch
        {
            DependencyType.FinishToStart =>
                $"Waiting for '{GetNodeName(predecessor)}' to complete",
            
            DependencyType.StartToStart =>
                $"Waiting for '{GetNodeName(predecessor)}' to start",
            
            _ => "Dependency constraint not satisfied"
        };
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 180 - Dependency Visualization**

### 180.1 Graph Rendering

```csharp
public class DependencyGraphVisualizer
{
    public string GenerateMermaidDiagram(DependencyGraph graph)
    {
        var sb = new StringBuilder();
        
        sb.AppendLine("```mermaid");
        sb.AppendLine("graph TD");
        
        // Add nodes
        foreach (var node in graph.Nodes)
        {
            var shape = GetNodeShape(node);
            var style = GetNodeStyle(node);
            
            sb.AppendLine($"    {GetNodeId(node)}[\"{GetNodeLabel(node)}\"] {shape}");
            
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(style))
            {
                sb.AppendLine($"    style {GetNodeId(node)} {style}");
            }
        }
        
        // Add edges
        foreach (var edge in graph.Edges)
        {
            var from = GetNodeId(graph.GetNode(edge.FromNodeId));
            var to = GetNodeId(graph.GetNode(edge.ToNodeId));
            var label = GetEdgeLabel(edge);
            var style = GetEdgeStyle(edge);
            
            sb.AppendLine($"    {from} -->{label} {to}");
            
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(style))
            {
                sb.AppendLine($"    linkStyle {style}");
            }
        }
        
        sb.AppendLine("```");
        
        return sb.ToString();
    }
    
    private string GetNodeShape(DependencyNode node)
    {
        if (node.IsComplete())
            return ":::complete";
        
        if (node.Status == NodeStatus.InProgress)
            return ":::inProgress";
        
        if (node.Status == NodeStatus.Blocked)
            return ":::blocked";
        
        return "";
    }
    
    private string GetEdgeLabel(DependencyEdge edge)
    {
        var parts = new List<string>();
        
        parts.Add(GetDependencyTypeAbbreviation(edge.Type));
        
        if (edge.Lag != Duration.Zero)
        {
            parts.Add($"lag:{edge.Lag.TotalDays:F0}d");
        }
        
        if (edge.IsOptional)
        {
            parts.Add("optional");
        }
        
        return $"|{string.Join(",", parts)}|";
    }
}

## **Chapter 182 - Performance Optimization**

### 182.1 Graph Caching

```csharp
public class DependencyGraphCacheService
{
    private readonly IDistributedCache _cache;
    
    public async Task<DependencyGraph> GetOrBuildGraphAsync(
        string context,
        Guid contextId)
    {
        var cacheKey = $"dep_graph:{context}:{contextId}";
        
        var cached = await _cache.GetAsync<DependencyGraph>(cacheKey);
        if (cached != null)
            return cached;
        
        // Build graph from database
        var graph = await BuildGraphFromDatabaseAsync(context, contextId);
        
        // Cache for 1 hour
        await _cache.SetAsync(
            cacheKey,
            graph,
            TimeSpan.FromHours(1));
        
        return graph;
    }
    
    public async Task InvalidateGraphAsync(string context, Guid contextId)
    {
        var cacheKey = $"dep_graph:{context}:{contextId}";
        await _cache.RemoveAsync(cacheKey);
    }
}
```

### 182.2 Incremental Updates

```csharp
public class IncrementalGraphUpdater
{
    public async Task UpdateNodeAsync(
        DependencyGraph graph,
        DependencyNode updatedNode)
    {
        // Only recalculate affected paths, not entire graph
        var affectedNodes = FindAffectedNodes(graph, updatedNode.Id);
        
        foreach (var nodeId in affectedNodes)
        {
            await RecalculateNodeAsync(graph, nodeId);
        }
    }
    
    private List<Guid> FindAffectedNodes(
        DependencyGraph graph,
        Guid changedNodeId)
    {
        var affected = new List<Guid>();
        var visited = new HashSet<Guid>();
        var queue = new Queue<Guid>();
        
        queue.Enqueue(changedNodeId);
        
        while (queue.Any())
        {
            var nodeId = queue.Dequeue();
            
            if (visited.Contains(nodeId))
                continue;
            
            visited.Add(nodeId);
            affected.Add(nodeId);
            
            // Add all successors
            var node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
            foreach (var edge in node.OutgoingEdges)
            {
                queue.Enqueue(edge.ToNodeId);
            }
        }
        
        return affected;
    }
}
```

## **Chapter 183 - Timeline Kernel Overview**

### 183.1 Purpose and Scope

The Timeline & History Kernel provides **unified event tracking and audit capabilities** across all bounded contexts, enabling:

- Complete audit trail of all entity changes
- Activity stream and feed generation
- Compliance and regulatory reporting
- Event sourcing capabilities
- Change history reconstruction
- User activity tracking
- System-wide timeline queries
- Forensic analysis and debugging

**Used By:**
- All bounded contexts (universal)
- Audit & Compliance systems
- Notification & Activity Feed
- Analytics & Reporting
- Security & Monitoring
- Debugging & Support tools

### 183.2 Core Value Proposition

**Problem Without Timeline Kernel:**
- Scattered audit logs across contexts
- Inconsistent change tracking
- Difficult to answer "what happened?" questions
- No unified activity feed
- Hard to trace causality chains
- Compliance gaps

**Solution With Timeline Kernel:**
- Single source of truth for all changes
- Consistent event schema
- Unified query interface
- Complete causality tracking
- Compliance-ready audit trail
- Rich activity streams

### 183.3 Timeline Architecture

```mermaid

    end

## **Chapter 184 - Timeline Entry Domain Model**

### 184.1 Core Entity Structure

```mermaid
classDiagram

    class ChangeSet {
        +string EntityType

    }
    
    class FieldChange {
        +string FieldPath
        +object OldValue

    }

        <<enumeration>>
        EntityCreated

    }
    
    TimelineEntry "1" --> "1" ChangeSet
    ChangeSet "1" --> "*" FieldChange
    TimelineEntry "1" --> "1" EventCategory
```

### 184.2 Timeline Entry Invariants

**Entry-Level Invariants:**
- Timestamp must be valid and not in future
- EntityType and EntityId required
- ActorId required for user-initiated events
- EventType must match Category
- CorrelationId required for tracking related events
- TenantId required for multi-tenancy isolation

**ChangeSet Invariants:**
- At least one field change required for Update events
- BeforeSnapshot and AfterSnapshot must be valid JSON
- Field paths must be valid dot-notation
- OldValue and NewValue types must match field type

**Event Chain Invariants:**
- CausationId must reference existing event if present
- ParentEventId must reference valid parent
- Version must increment sequentially for same entity

## **Chapter 186 - Event Collection and Transformation**

### 186.1 Event Collector Service

```csharp
public class TimelineEventCollector
{
    private readonly IEventBus _eventBus;
    private readonly ITimelineRepository _repository;
    private readonly IEventEnricher _enricher;
    private readonly ICurrentUser _currentUser;
    
    public async Task CollectAsync(DomainEvent domainEvent)
    {
        // Transform domain event to timeline entry
        var entry = await TransformToTimelineEntryAsync(domainEvent);
        
        // Enrich with additional context
        entry = await _enricher.EnrichAsync(entry);
        
        // Persist
        await _repository.InsertAsync(entry);
        
        // Publish to event bus for consumers
        await _eventBus.PublishAsync(new TimelineEntryCreatedEto
        {
            EntryId = entry.Id,
            EntityType = entry.EntityType,
            EntityId = entry.EntityId,
            EventType = entry.EventType,
            Timestamp = entry.Timestamp
        });
    }
    
    private async Task<TimelineEntry> TransformToTimelineEntryAsync(
        DomainEvent domainEvent)
    {
        var entry = new TimelineEntry
        {
            Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
            TenantId = _currentUser.TenantId ?? Guid.Empty,
            Timestamp = domainEvent.OccurredAt,
            EntityType = domainEvent.EntityType,
            EntityId = domainEvent.EntityId,
            EventType = domainEvent.EventName,
            Category = DetermineCategory(domainEvent.EventName),
            ActorId = _currentUser.UserId,
            ActorType = "User",
            ActorName = _currentUser.UserName,
            Source = domainEvent.Source ?? "Application",
            CorrelationId = domainEvent.CorrelationId,
            CausationId = domainEvent.CausationId,
            Metadata = domainEvent.Metadata,
            Version = 1
        };
        
        // Build description
        entry.Description = await BuildDescriptionAsync(domainEvent);
        
        // Extract change set if available
        if (domainEvent is EntityChangedEvent changedEvent)
        {
            entry.ChangeSet = ExtractChangeSet(changedEvent);
        }
        
        return entry;
    }
    
    private EventCategory DetermineCategory(string eventType)
    {
        if (eventType.EndsWith(".created"))
            return EventCategory.EntityCreated;
        
        if (eventType.EndsWith(".updated"))
            return EventCategory.EntityUpdated;
        
        if (eventType.EndsWith(".deleted") || eventType.EndsWith(".archived"))
            return EventCategory.EntityDeleted;
        
        if (eventType.Contains(".status_"))
            return EventCategory.StatusChanged;
        
        if (eventType.Contains(".assigned") || eventType.Contains(".delegated"))
            return EventCategory.AssignmentChanged;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("workflow."))
            return EventCategory.WorkflowTransition;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("approval."))
            return EventCategory.ApprovalDecision;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("comment."))
            return EventCategory.CommentAdded;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("attachment."))
            return EventCategory.AttachmentAdded;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("dependency.") || eventType.Contains("relationship."))
            return EventCategory.RelationshipChanged;
        
        if (eventType.Contains("security."))
            return EventCategory.SecurityEvent;
        
        return EventCategory.SystemEvent;
    }
}
```

### 186.2 Event Enricher

```csharp
public class TimelineEventEnricher : IEventEnricher
{
    private readonly IUserRepository _userRepo;
    private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContext;
    
    public async Task<TimelineEntry> EnrichAsync(TimelineEntry entry)
    {
        // Enrich actor information
        if (entry.ActorId.HasValue)
        {
            var user = await _userRepo.GetAsync(entry.ActorId.Value);
            if (user != null)
            {
                entry.ActorName = user.FullName;
                entry.Metadata["actor_email"] = user.Email;
                entry.Metadata["actor_roles"] = user.Roles;
            }
        }
        
        // Add HTTP context if available
        if (_httpContext.HttpContext != null)
        {
            entry.SourceIP = _httpContext.HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString();
            entry.UserAgent = _httpContext.HttpContext.Request.Headers["User-Agent"].ToString();
            entry.Metadata["request_path"] = _httpContext.HttpContext.Request.Path.ToString();
            entry.Metadata["request_method"] = _httpContext.HttpContext.Request.Method;
        }
        
        // Add entity metadata
        await EnrichEntityMetadataAsync(entry);
        
        // Add correlation chain
        await EnrichCorrelationChainAsync(entry);
        
        return entry;
    }
    
    private async Task EnrichEntityMetadataAsync(TimelineEntry entry)
    {
        // Add entity-specific context
        switch (entry.EntityType)
        {
            case "Task":
                var task = await _taskRepo.GetAsync(entry.EntityId);
                if (task != null)
                {
                    entry.Metadata["task_title"] = task.Title;
                    entry.Metadata["task_status"] = task.Status;
                    entry.Metadata["project_id"] = task.ProjectId;
                }
                break;
                
            case "Project":
                var project = await _projectRepo.GetAsync(entry.EntityId);
                if (project != null)
                {
                    entry.Metadata["project_title"] = project.Title;
                    entry.Metadata["project_status"] = project.Status;
                }
                break;
        }
    }
    
    private async Task EnrichCorrelationChainAsync(TimelineEntry entry)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(entry.CorrelationId))
            return;
        
        // Find root event
        var rootEvent = await _repository.FindRootEventAsync(entry.CorrelationId);
        if (rootEvent != null)
        {
            entry.Metadata["root_event_id"] = rootEvent.Id;
            entry.Metadata["root_event_type"] = rootEvent.EventType;
            entry.Metadata["chain_depth"] = await CalculateChainDepthAsync(entry);
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp
public class TimelineDescriptionBuilder
{
    public async Task<string> BuildDescriptionAsync(DomainEvent domainEvent)
    {
        return domainEvent.EventName switch
        {
            "task.created" => 
                $"Created task '{GetTaskTitle(domainEvent)}'",
            
            "task.assigned" =>
                $"Assigned task to {GetUserName(domainEvent.Metadata["assignee_id"])}",
            
            "task.status_changed" =>
                $"Changed status from {domainEvent.Metadata["old_status"]} " +
                $"to {domainEvent.Metadata["new_status"]}",
            
            "task.completed" =>
                $"Completed task '{GetTaskTitle(domainEvent)}'",
            
            "comment.added" =>
                $"Added comment: \"{TruncateText(domainEvent.Metadata["comment_text"], 100)}\"",
            
            "approval.decision_made" =>
                $"{domainEvent.Metadata["decision"]} approval request",
            
            "workflow.transitioned" =>
                $"Transitioned from {domainEvent.Metadata["from_status"]} " +
                $"to {domainEvent.Metadata["to_status"]} via '{domainEvent.Metadata["transition_name"]}'",
            
            "dependency.added" =>
                $"Added dependency: {GetTaskTitle(domainEvent)} depends on " +
                $"{GetTaskTitle(domainEvent.Metadata["depends_on_task_id"])}",
            
            _ => GenerateDefaultDescription(domainEvent)
        };
    }
    
    private string GenerateDefaultDescription(DomainEvent domainEvent)
    {
        var action = ExtractAction(domainEvent.EventName);
        return $"{action} {domainEvent.EntityType.ToLower()}";
    }
    
    private string ExtractAction(string eventName)
    {
        var parts = eventName.Split('.');
        if (parts.Length > 1)
        {
            return parts[1].Replace("_", " ").Capitalize();
        }
        return eventName;
    }
}
